items.citation:
# Citation

Candidate record for JSP-000840 — Lean formalization of Rademacher's theorem (l = 1 case). This is not an award; verification is under review.

## English

**Status**: candidate, under verification. No award decision is claimed.

**Result formalized.** Every graph on `n ≥ 3` vertices with at least `⌊n²/4⌋ + 1` edges contains at least `⌊n/2⌋` triangles (Rademacher, 1962). The proof was formalized in Lean 4 (v4.33.0, mathlib `db584cd6`) as `Rad.rademacher` in the public repository https://github.com/aichiwuhuarou/rademacher-lean, first pushed 2026-09-17T14:42Z. The formalization is a strong induction on the vertex count using mathlib's Turán machinery for Mantel's theorem, handshake-lemma degree arguments, vertex deletion, and a degree-excess pigeonhole; full details are in the repository's README and PROOF.md.

**Scope.** The catalogued entry records the general answer of Khadzhiivanov–Nikiforov (1981): `⌊n²/4⌋ + l` edges force at least `⌊n/2⌋ · l` triangles for `2l < n`. This candidate formalizes the `l = 1` case only. The general case requires the long structural proof of Lovász–Simonovits and is not included; accordingly this candidate is submitted as partial coverage of the entry, not as a completed formalization of the general theorem.

**Evidence.** The repository builds locally (`lake build`, all targets) and independently on GitHub Actions (`leanprover/lean-action@v1`, run `35235416616`, 15m26s, passed; log archived as a commit-pinned blob inside the repository). The axiom audit reports only `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`, reproducible with the repository's `Audit.lean`. A prior-art search on 2026-09-17 found no existing Lean formalization of this theorem (statement or proof) anywhere.

**Attribution.** The theorem is due to E. Rademacher (1962, unpublished). The formalization was produced with AI assistance (GLM, via the ZCode agent) under the direction of the declarant `aichiwuhuarou`, a natural person; all Lean scripts are original to the repository. Recipient confirmation and identity verification remain pending, so recipients are listed under a placeholder in `recipients.md`.

A registration application for the same formalization was previously filed as issue #792; this candidate record is the formal channel counterpart referenced there.

statement_comparison.basis: The candidate statement (STMT-jsp-000840-v1) is the l = 1 case of the catalogued problem: every graph on n ≥ 3 vertices with at least n²/4 + 1 edges contains at least n/2 triangles (floors in natural division). The Lean theorem Rad.rademacher states exactly this, with hypotheses h3 : 3 ≤ Fintype.card V and he : Fintype.card V ^ 2 / 4 + 1 ≤ G.edgeFinset.card and conclusion Fintype.card V / 2 ≤ (G.cliqueFinset 3).card; edge counting is via mathlib's edgeFinset and triangle counting via cliqueFinset 3. Quantifier structure and all premises match clause by clause. The general l case recorded in the entry (Khadzhiivanov-Nikiforov) is NOT covered by this theorem; see citation.md for the scope statement.

attribution.proof_route: Strong induction on the number of vertices following Rademacher (1962): handshake-lemma degree arguments to peel a low-degree vertex, Mantel's theorem (via mathlib's Turán machinery) for base cases and the no-triangle subcase, edge deletion for the even-order subcase, and the sum-of-degree-excess pigeonhole for the minimum-degree case. The informal write-up (PROOF.md in the repository) was assembled from public lecture materials with all numerical identities re-derived and three gaps in a widely circulated transcription repaired.
attribution.note_en: Formalization produced with AI assistance (GLM, via the ZCode agent) under the direction of the declarant aichiwuhuarou; all Lean scripts are original to the repository and no third-party Lean code was copied. Axiom audit via #print axioms / Lean.collectAxioms reports only [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]; there is no sorry, native_decide, or custom axiom.

statement.natural_language_source: Justin Sun Prize problem bank entry JSP-000840: 'How many triangles must a graph have once its edge count exceeds the maximum bipartite edge count?' The formalized statement is the l = 1 case: every graph on n ≥ 3 vertices with at least floor(n²/4) + 1 edges contains at least floor(n/2) triangles (Rademacher, 1962). The general l case (floor(n²/4) + l edges force floor(n/2)·l triangles, Khadzhiivanov-Nikiforov 1981) is not part of this statement.

definitions_reviewed.name: SimpleGraph.edgeFinset.card (edge count)
definitions_reviewed.review: mathlib's canonical edge Finset; its cardinality is the graph's edge count. Division by 4 in ℕ is truncating, so Fintype.card V ^ 2 / 4 is floor(n²/4), matching the Mantel/Turán threshold.

definitions_reviewed.name: SimpleGraph.cliqueFinset 3 (triangles)
definitions_reviewed.review: mathlib's canonical encoding of triangles as 3-cliques; cardinality counts triangles exactly.
